reason: The cited evidence confirms that Al2O3 and Cr2O3 are protective oxides and that Al2O3 scales grow slower and are more stable (E2), but it does not directly support the claim that increasing Al and Cr content in HEAs necessarily leads to a more compact, adherent scale via the proposed diffusion mechanism, nor does it provide comparative data against a baseline alloy. E1 and E3 discuss specific alloy behaviors and oxide formation but do not establish the general mechanistic link between higher Al/Cr content and improved scale properties.
premises: Increasing Al and Cr content promotes formation of protective Al2O3 and Cr2O3 scales
Al2O3 and Cr2O3 scales are dense, adherent, and slow-growing
Slower metal outward diffusion relative to oxygen inward diffusion leads to a compact oxide barrier
Higher Al/Cr alloys will show lower oxidation weight gain and more uniform oxide layers than baseline alloys
The mechanism applies to HEAs exposed above 900 °C for >48–100 hours
